locations.description: The medieval castle Salvador Dalí bought and decorated for his wife Gala — golden throne room, surrealist details, Gala's crypt. 'Such a fun museum!' A 30-minute drive inland from Begur; the best culture wildcard of the area with the Dalí Triangle beyond it.

locations.name: Cala Sa Tuna
locations.description: Tiny, postcard cove below Begur ringed by old fishermen's houses with brightly painted doors — now the consensus cove of the research: Gemini's top-three pick plus heart-icon favorite or must-see in three separate Instagram posts. Deep emerald water, great snorkeling, and the waterfront tavern is pinned down: Restaurante Sa Tuna on the promenade, with Es Furió's arroz mar steps away.

locations.name: Cala Aiguablava
locations.description: One of the rare Costa Brava calas with genuinely fine sand and famously bright-blue water — heart-icon favorite in the Begur guide and named in three posts of the Instagram batch, on top of Gemini's original endorsement. Home to Toc al Mar on the sand, with Cap Sa Sal on the cliffs above and tiny Platja d'en Malaret next door: the densest single-bay cluster of the whole Costa Brava list.

locations.name: Toc al Mar
locations.description: Beach restaurant directly on the sand at Cala Aiguablava — whole fish and paella over an oak-wood fire, long barefoot-luxury lunches. Recommended in two separate Gemini/Manus AI conversations and now the Instagram Begur guide too ('Toca al Mar — paella'). Reservations coveted; book well ahead for early September.

locations.name: Begur
locations.description: Hilltop town crowned by a castle and the epicenter of Costa Brava recommendations across every source — the batch-2 Instagram sweep confirms it plays the role Deià/Sóller play in Mallorca. Base for the best calas (Sa Tuna, Aiguablava, Fonda, Malaret, Aiguafreda, Illa Roja all within 10 minutes), with the densest restaurant cluster of the coast in and around town.
